title: Alternating-form dimension
statement:
Let $K$ be a field with $\operatorname{char}(K)\neq2$, $V$ a
finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, and $\beta:V\times V\to K$ a
nondegenerate alternating bilinear form. Then $\dim_K V$ is even.

proof.text: Choose a basis b of V indexed by a finite type ι with |ι|=n=dim_K V  (for example, a basis indexed by Fin n), and let B be the Gram matrix of β in b. Alternation gives B^\top=-B. Therefore det(B)=det(B^\top)=det(-B)=(-1)^n det(B), using invariance of determinant under transpose and the determinant of a negated matrix; the exponent is n because the basis index has cardinality n. By the cited nondegeneracy criterion, det(B)\ne0. Cancelling this nonzero factor yields (-1)^n=1. If n were odd, then (-1)^n=-1, so 1=-1 and hence 2=0 in K, contradicting char(K)\ne2. Thus n is even, as required.
